name: Keto Grocery Checklist
description: A ketogenic shopping list organized by category, from healthy fats and proteins to low-carb veg, dairy and pantry staples.

items.note: Fats are the backbone of a keto plate.

items.text: Fatty fish like salmon, mackerel and sardines
Bacon and sausage with no added sugar
items.note: Check labels, as some cured meats add sugar.

items.text: Tofu and tempeh for plant-based protein

items.note: Stick to non-starchy veg that grow above ground.

items.text: Full-fat plain Greek yogurt in moderation

items.note: Choose unsweetened versions to avoid added sugar.

items.text: Nut butter with no added sugar
Sugar-free sweetener such as erythritol or stevia

items.note: Pantry staples make keto cooking easier and more varied.

items.text: Electrolytes or extra salt for the early adjustment
Pickles and low-sugar condiments like mustard
Dark chocolate (high cacao) as an occasional treat
Important: this is general information, not medical or dietary advice
items.note: Keto is a medical-style diet — consult your doctor or a registered dietitian before starting, especially with a health condition.

faq.a: The ketogenic diet is a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat way of eating, typically keeping carbs around 20 to 50 grams a day. The aim is to shift the body toward burning fat for fuel. It relies on fats, protein and low-carb vegetables while avoiding sugar and starches.

faq.q: What foods do you avoid on keto?
faq.a: You avoid sugar, sugary drinks, bread, pasta, rice, potatoes, most grains, beans, and high-sugar fruits. Many processed and packaged foods are too high in carbs as well, so reading labels for total carbs is important.
Non-starchy vegetables that grow above ground are best: leafy greens, broccoli, cauliflower, zucchini, peppers, asparagus and mushrooms. Limit starchy vegetables like potatoes, corn and peas.

faq.q: Can I print this keto grocery checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF to take to the store, ticking off each keto staple by category as you shop.

Keto is not right for everyone. This is general information, not medical or dietary advice. If you have diabetes, take medication, are pregnant or have a health condition, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian before starting keto.
